monocyte cells, in the breast tumor environment, play an important role on the modulation of MMP's.

the interaction of monocytes and breast carcinoma cells.
the role of monocyte cells in breast cancer progression.
the interaction between monocyte cells and breast cancer cells in the tumor microenvironment.

the monocytes are able to produce a variety of cytokines and growth factors that are involved in the growth and progression of breast cancer cells.

monocytes play an important role within the breast cancer tumor microenvironment, in which they are capable of secreting matrix metalloproteinases, which in turn, are capable of modulating the invasive potential of breast cancer cells.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
monocytes are able to modulate MMP-2 in a paracrine fashion in breast adenocarcinaoma cells.
breast tumor cells can modulate monocytes in a way that increases MMP-2 and TIMP-1, which may promote tumor growth and metastasis.
breast cancer cells can induce monocytes to produce MMP-2, which can then promote tumor invasion and metastasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of monocyte cells in growing breast cancer is not simply a bystander effect.
the monocyte is an important cell that is present in breast tumors.
monocytes are not bystanders, but rather active participants in the growth and spread of breast cancer.
